financials_interim.company_name: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka and Finance PLC
financials_interim.notes: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka and Finance PLC (MBSL) is a Bank of Ceylon-controlled licensed finance company; this filing presents both Company and Group columns -- Group consolidates one subsidiary (MBSL Insurance Company Ltd) and equity-accounts one associate (Lanka Securities Ltd), so basis=GROUP is entered (not Company). MBSL's financial year is calendar (Jan-Dec, confirmed by the SOFP comparative '12/31/2025 (Audited)'), so this filing's 'quarter ended 30 June 2026' is fiscal Q2, not Q1 -- distinct from AAF/CDB/LOFC/MERC/PMB/LOLC in this batch which all run an April-March fiscal year. The filing discloses BOTH a discrete 'Quarter ended' column and a cumulative 'Six months ended' column for the income statement; per this project's quarterly convention the DISCRETE QUARTER (Apr-Jun 2026) Group figures are entered here, which also keeps the YoY comparison on a like-for-like quarter-vs-same-quarter-last-year basis (p.3). Per NBFI convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (642,385 thousand, Group quarter), the filing's own top-line subtotal after net interest income + net fee income + insurance result + trading/FV/other income; operating_profit = 'Profit/(loss) from operations after impairment from subsidiary investments' (-175,786), the filing's own subtotal before taxes on financial services; profit_before_tax = 'Profit/(loss) before income tax' (-215,004), which already includes the share of associate (Lanka Securities) profit of 12,108; tax_expense = 'Income tax expense/(reversal)' (-12,570, a net tax credit/reversal this quarter); profit_after_tax = 'Profit/(loss) for the period' (-202,434); minority_interest = -39,051 (NCI's share of the quarterly loss, i.e. NCI absorbed part of the loss -- equity holders' share was -163,383). MBSL swung to a loss this quarter (Group PBT -215,004 vs +174,743 a year ago) -- the single largest driver is 'Net gain/(loss) from trading', which swung from a Rs.292,922k GAIN in Q2 2025 to a Rs.38,812k LOSS in Q2 2026 (a Rs.331,734k negative swing), combined with 'Other operating income' swinging from +Rs.25,186k to -Rs.24,345k (a further Rs.49,531k negative swing) -- both booked in the 'Total operating income' line (p.3). This is compounded by the impairment line flipping from a Rs.55,356k REVERSAL in Q2 2025 to an Rs.80,630k CHARGE in Q2 2026 (a Rs.135,986k negative swing) and a rise in D&A (+15.1% to Rs.93,027k). Net interest income actually IMPROVED (+10.3% to Rs.831,536k, as interest income grew 25.9% to Rs.2,151,081k outpacing interest expense growth of 38.1% to Rs.1,319,545k off a smaller base) -- so the loss is a trading/impairment story, not a core lending-margin story. The filing itself (p.8, Basis of preparation) discloses a material regulatory constraint: the Central Bank imposed restrictions from 17 April 2026 (non-compliance with capital adequacy) capping new lending (except cash-back/pawning/gold loans up to 70% LTV) and capping outstanding deposits at Rs.35bn, pending the Company's return to compliance -- disclosed here as important operating context, not reflected as a P&L line. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank -- liquidity-ordered SOFP, no current/non-current split, and 'Loans & receivables at amortised cost' (Rs.38,667,843k) is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks' (10,840,118); long_term_borrowings = 'Debt issued and borrowed funds at amortised cost' (1,753,361), which per the debenture note (p.12) is entirely listed subordinated debentures maturing 2027-2030, genuinely long-dated. 'Due to customers at amortised cost' (34,005,940, deposits) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt. total_equity = equity attributable to the parent (4,149,251) -- ties exactly to disclosed Group NAV/share of Rs.7.91 (4,149,251k/524,539,637 shares = 7.91); Group NCI balance of Rs.249,380k as at 30 June 2026 is NOT separately captured by this schema (only the period's NCI P&L share is, via minority_interest) -- noted here for completeness. shares_in_issue = 524,539,637 (Number of shares issued, p.13), cross-checked: EPS basic (loss) -0.31 = -163,383,000/524,539,637 = -0.3115, ties. Cash flow figures (p.7) are NOT split by quarter -- the statement only presents cumulative SIX-MONTH figures (Jan-Jun 2026 vs Jan-Jun 2025), so cash_from_operations/investing/financing entered here are six-month cumulative Group figures, NOT isolated-quarter figures like the income-statement lines above -- flagged as a genuine presentation gap (same issue encountered with LOFC/CDB in this project). capex = Purchase of PPE (57,160) + Acquisition of intangible assets (292,690) = 349,850 (six-month cumulative, Group).

interim_updates.company_name: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka and Finance PLC
interim_updates.note_text: Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka and Finance PLC (MBSL, Group, discrete quarter ended 30 June 2026) swung to a loss this quarter: Profit/(loss) before income tax fell to Rs.(215.00)mn from Rs.174.74mn a year earlier (-223.0% YoY), and Profit/(loss) for the period fell to Rs.(202.43)mn from Rs.72.42mn (-379.5% YoY); Total operating income fell 33.0% to Rs.642.39mn from Rs.958.33mn. The single largest driver is 'Net gain/(loss) from trading', which swung from a Rs.292.92mn GAIN in Q2 2025 to a Rs.38.81mn LOSS in Q2 2026 -- a Rs.331.73mn negative swing -- compounded by 'Other operating income' swinging from +Rs.25.19mn to -Rs.24.35mn (a further Rs.49.53mn negative swing), both embedded in the Total operating income line. This is compounded by the impairment line flipping from a Rs.55.36mn REVERSAL in Q2 2025 to an Rs.80.63mn CHARGE in Q2 2026 (a Rs.135.99mn negative swing) and Depreciation and amortisation rising 15.1% to Rs.93.03mn. Importantly, Net interest income actually IMPROVED 10.3% YoY to Rs.831.54mn, as Interest and similar income grew 25.9% to Rs.2,151.08mn, outpacing Interest and similar expense growth of 38.1% to Rs.1,319.55mn off a smaller base -- so the loss is a trading-book and impairment story, not a core lending-margin story. Income tax expense/(reversal) swung to a Rs.12.57mn net credit this quarter from a Rs.102.32mn charge PY, partially offsetting the larger pretax loss. Operating margin fell to -27.4% from +29.3%, and net margin fell to -31.5% from +7.6%. Separately and materially, the filing's Basis of Preparation note (p.8) discloses that the Central Bank of Sri Lanka imposed regulatory restrictions on MBSL from 17 April 2026 for non-compliance with capital adequacy requirements -- capping new lending (except cash-back/pawning/gold loans up to 70% LTV) and capping outstanding deposits at Rs.35bn, pending the Company's return to compliance. This is disclosed as important operating context but is not itself a P&L line item this quarter.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is MBSL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the cash flow statement (p.7) is NOT split by discrete quarter -- only cumulative SIX-MONTH figures (Jan-Jun 2026 vs Jan-Jun 2025) are presented, so the cash_from_operations/investing/financing figures already stored in financial_statements for this period are six-month cumulative, not isolated-quarter, and are NOT used in this quarter's YoY income-statement comparison above; (2) no qualitative commentary in the filing explains the specific instruments/positions behind the Rs.331.73mn negative swing in 'Net gain/(loss) from trading' -- the trading-book composition driving this swing is not disclosed; (3) the CBSL regulatory restriction (capital-adequacy non-compliance, effective 17 April 2026, capping new lending and deposits at Rs.35bn) is disclosed only qualitatively (p.8, Basis of Preparation) with no quantified P&L or balance-sheet impact attributed to it in this filing -- a genuine disclosure gap given its evident materiality to the going-forward outlook.
interim_updates.takeaway: MBSL's swing to a Rs.(202.43)mn Group loss this quarter (from a Rs.72.42mn profit a year earlier) is a trading-book and impairment story, not a core-lending-margin story: Net interest income actually improved 10.3% YoY. The dominant driver is the Rs.331.73mn negative swing in Net gain/(loss) from trading (Rs.292.92mn gain to Rs.38.81mn loss), compounded by a Rs.135.99mn negative swing in impairment (reversal to charge) and a Rs.49.53mn negative swing in other operating income. The Central Bank's capital-adequacy-driven restrictions on new lending and deposit growth (effective 17 April 2026, disclosed p.8) are a material qualitative overhang for the outlook that is not yet quantified in this filing's P&L, and should be weighed alongside the quarter's trading losses when assessing near-term recovery prospects.

operational_highlights: Group Total operating income Rs.642.39mn, -33.0% YoY (Q2 2025: Rs.958.33mn); Profit/(loss) before income tax Rs.(215.00)mn, -223.0% YoY (Q2 2025: Rs.174.74mn); Profit/(loss) for the period Rs.(202.43)mn, -379.5% YoY (Q2 2025: Rs.72.42mn); EPS Rs.(0.31) (Q2 2025: Rs.0.19).
Net gain/(loss) from trading swung from a Rs.292.92mn GAIN to a Rs.38.81mn LOSS YoY, a Rs.331.73mn negative swing -- the single largest driver of the quarter's loss.
Impairment charge/(reversal) flipped from a Rs.55.36mn REVERSAL (Q2 2025) to an Rs.80.63mn CHARGE (Q2 2026), a Rs.135.99mn negative swing.

Net interest income improved 10.3% YoY to Rs.831.54mn (interest income +25.9% to Rs.2,151.08mn outpacing interest expense +38.1% to Rs.1,319.55mn) -- the core lending margin was not the source of the loss.

Central Bank of Sri Lanka imposed capital-adequacy-related restrictions from 17 April 2026 capping new lending (ex. cash-back/pawning/gold loans up to 70% LTV) and outstanding deposits at Rs.35bn (p.8).
key_drivers: Net gain/(loss) from trading swing of Rs.331.73mn (Rs.292.92mn gain to Rs.38.81mn loss YoY) is the single largest driver of the quarter's loss.
Impairment charge/(reversal) swing of Rs.135.99mn (Rs.55.36mn reversal to Rs.80.63mn charge YoY) is the second-largest driver.
Other operating income swing of Rs.49.53mn (+Rs.25.19mn to -Rs.24.35mn YoY) is a smaller but compounding negative driver, also embedded in Total operating income.
Core lending economics were NOT a driver of the loss -- Net interest income improved 10.3% YoY to Rs.831.54mn.
